claims.claim: Bayesian scattering with topological-sensitivity priors and unknown-object-count model selection predates B1.
claims.evidence: Abstract describes topological sensitivity for prior construction, 2D synthetic holography, MCMC/linearized Gaussian posterior comparison, and stochastic model selection for unknown object number.
claims.b1_implication: Attribute these general ideas; this abstract establishes neither B1 internal-cavity support nor calibrated 3D vector-Maxwell probabilities.

claims.claim: For a fixed linear projector, conditional expectation of the likelihood gives a KL-optimal profile in the specified reduced posterior family.
claims.evidence: Section 2.1 defines the conditional-likelihood posterior and decomposes KL error into its minimum plus remaining profile error, equations (4)–(7).
claims.study_context: General Bayesian density reduction relative to a common prior.
claims.b1_implication: Conditional-likelihood integration and its generic KL profile optimality need existing attribution; this does not certify B1 topology mixture or nonlinear Maxwell signature.

claims.claim: Zahm et al. obtain posterior approximation bounds under explicit prior/likelihood regularity assumptions.
claims.evidence: Abstract and section 2.2 use logarithmic Sobolev conditions and log-likelihood gradient moments; section 2.2 states assumptions on prior support and density.
claims.study_context: Nonlinear/non-Gaussian inverse problems subject to stated assumptions.
claims.b1_implication: No transfer of the certified label to empirical polynomial interpolation without checking assumptions and constructing a B1 remainder bound.

claims.claim: Sparse/decomposable transport maps for low-dimensional non-Gaussian inference have established prior work.
claims.evidence: JMLR abstract connects target Markov properties to sparse or decomposable couplings and discusses nonlinear filtering, smoothing, and parameter inference.
claims.study_context: Continuous non-Gaussian graphical models; general transport theory.
claims.confidence_reason: Official journal abstract and bibliography agree.
claims.b1_implication: Do not claim low-dimensional transport itself as new; B1 has no NN transport implementation in this scope.

claims.claim: Defensive mixture importance sampling is an established device for protecting importance weights.
claims.evidence: Publisher abstract explains that including the original target distribution in the sampling mixture bounds weights and improves reliability.
claims.confidence_reason: Original publisher abstract indexed; direct full-text access failed.
claims.b1_implication: B1 uses its proper prior as the defensive component and explicitly corrects by prior/proposal density. Literature attribution does not prove that 16 samples per branch find all posterior modes.

claims.claim: Multilayer-sphere electromagnetic Mie computation is existing physical methodology.
claims.evidence: Abstract presents scattnlay as an implementation of Yang’s multilayer-sphere algorithm; program summary specifies Mie coefficients/amplitudes, single scattering, and unit layer permeability.
claims.study_context: Radially layered single spheres; nonmagnetic layers.
claims.confidence_reason: Original publisher abstract/program summary indexed; direct full text unavailable.
claims.b1_implication: Attribute layered Mie physics; this citation is neither independent validation of B1 code nor evidence for arbitrary-geometry imaging.

claims.claim: SBC validates Bayesian computation over an assumed prior-generative model using posterior rank statistics.
claims.evidence: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 draw prior parameters, simulated observations, and posterior samples, then compare rank histograms with discrete-uniform behavior.
claims.study_context: Computational consistency under a specified generative model.
claims.locator: v2, printed pp.4–6, section 4 and Algorithm 1
claims.b1_implication: B1 currently reports probability bins, proper scores, and credible coverage; a Talts-style posterior-rank SBC claim is not supported by those outputs alone.

claims.claim: SBC does not establish model adequacy or truth coverage for every individual observation.
claims.evidence: Section 4 limits calibration to computation and distinguishes it from sensitivity and posterior-predictive model checking.
claims.b1_implication: Keep model-conditional development calibration separate from external physical and representation validation.

unresolved_gaps.claim_not_supported: Global or first-in-field novelty for probabilistic Maxwell topology imaging.

unresolved_gaps.claim_not_supported: Uniformly certified full-Mie posterior or quadrature error.
unresolved_gaps.reason: Local refinement records explicitly retain no uniform interpolation remainder and four original full-grid reference failures.

unresolved_gaps.claim_not_supported: Unbiased finite-sample normalized topology probabilities, exhaustive mode discovery, or importance-sampling superiority.
unresolved_gaps.reason: Local importance receipt reports finite-N ratio bias and missed-mode limits; 48 evaluation proposal (16 per branch) differs from order7 topology probabilities by 0.02565392904725572.

unresolved_gaps.claim_not_supported: Talts-style posterior-rank SBC or real-world calibration.
unresolved_gaps.reason: Local calibration uses 24 material parents and 720 clustered noise realizations, probability bins/scores/coverage. It does not report posterior-rank histograms.

unresolved_gaps.claim_not_supported: Probability for arbitrary unknown geometry, unknown cavity position, or unmodeled topology.
unresolved_gaps.reason: Declared B1 prior is fixed radial topology templates with continuous complex-permittivity variables; source explicitly leaves unmodeled geometry mass undefined.

unresolved_gaps.reason: Metadata verified; abstract elided and direct publisher fetch403. Hesterberg abstract supports only the bounded defensive-mixture statement above.
